title: Module 6 · Infectious Diseases and Stewardship
intro: Sepsis timing and prolonged infusions, CAP, HAP and MRSA nares, cefepime toxicity, cUTI and asymptomatic bacteriuria, skin infections, meningitis, S. aureus and ESBL bacteremia, penicillin allergy, duplicates and the day 3 time out.

cases.title: Sepsis: the first hour
cases.stem: A 68 year old woman, BP 82/50 after fluids, lactate 4.6, likely pneumonia. Antibiotic orders arrive.

options.t: Within 1 hour of recognition, because shock is present
options.why: SSC 2021 strong recommendation. Without shock and when sepsis is only possible, within 3 hours after rapid assessment.

options.t: Within 6 hours
options.why: Too slow when shock is present.

steps.q: What do you do to make that happen?

options.t: Verify the first doses STAT and get them sent or pulled right away
options.why: Your verification speed is part of the clock.

options.t: Give the full first dose even if the kidneys look bad, then adjust later doses
options.why: Load by weight, maintain by kidneys.

options.t: Give the shortest infusion drug first when several are ordered (for example a beta lactam push or short piggyback before vancomycin)
options.why: The broad gram negative agent usually matters most in the first minutes; vancomycin takes longer to infuse.

options.t: Wait for cultures to result before starting
options.why: Draw cultures first if it does not delay antibiotics, but never wait for results.

cases.pearl: **Shock: antibiotics in 1 hour. Full first doses. Fastest drug first.**

sources.t: Evans L, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021. Crit Care Med 2021;49:e1063-e1143
St. Mary's antibiogram, sepsis order set and antimicrobial stewardship policies (verify locally)

cases.title: Prolonged beta lactam infusions
cases.stem: After the STAT first dose, the order is piperacillin tazobactam 4.5 g every 6 hours over 30 minutes.

steps.q: What does SSC 2021 suggest for beta lactam maintenance doses?

options.t: Prolonged (extended) infusion over standard infusion
options.why: Beta lactams kill based on time above the MIC; longer infusions keep levels above the MIC longer.

options.t: Faster push dosing

steps.q: Why does time matter for beta lactams but not as much for aminoglycosides?

options.t: Beta lactams are time dependent; aminoglycosides are concentration dependent
They are the same

cases.pearl: **Beta lactams: time above MIC. Prolonged infusion after the first dose.**

sources.t: Evans L, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021. Crit Care Med 2021;49:e1063-e1143
St. Mary's antibiogram, sepsis order set and antimicrobial stewardship policies (verify locally)

cases.title: Community acquired pneumonia on the floor
cases.stem: Moderate CAP, not ICU, no MRSA or Pseudomonas risk factors. No allergies.

options.t: Ceftriaxone 1 to 2 g IV daily plus azithromycin 500 mg daily
Levofloxacin 750 mg daily or moxifloxacin 400 mg daily alone
options.why: Respiratory fluoroquinolone monotherapy is an option.

options.t: Vancomycin plus piperacillin tazobactam
options.why: Too broad without MRSA or Pseudomonas risk.

options.t: At least 5 days, and until clinically stable
14 days
No; follow the sepsis guideline if refractory shock develops
Yes, always

cases.pearl: **CAP floor: ceftriaxone + azithromycin, or a respiratory FQ. 5 days.**

sources.t: Metlay JP, et al. ATS/IDSA community acquired pneumonia guideline. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2019;200:e45-e67

cases.title: MRSA nares and stopping vancomycin
cases.stem: Day 2 of vancomycin plus cefepime for pneumonia. MRSA nasal PCR is negative. Sputum culture grows normal flora.

options.t: Stop vancomycin: a negative MRSA nares result has a negative predictive value above 95% for MRSA pneumonia
options.why: One of the easiest stewardship wins every day.

options.t: Continue vancomycin for 14 days

cases.call: "The MRSA nares PCR is negative and the sputum has no MRSA. The negative predictive value is above 95%. May I stop vancomycin and continue cefepime?"
cases.pearl: **Negative MRSA nares + no MRSA in cultures = stop vanc for pneumonia.**

sources.t: Kalil AC, et al. IDSA/ATS HAP and VAP guideline. Clin Infect Dis 2016;63:e61-e111
St. Mary's antibiogram, sepsis order set and antimicrobial stewardship policies (verify locally)

cases.title: Hospital acquired pneumonia
cases.stem: New pneumonia on day 6. No shock, not ventilated, no IV antibiotics in 90 days, local MRSA rate under 20%.

steps.q: Which single agents fit IDSA/ATS for HAP without high risk features?

options.t: Piperacillin tazobactam 4.5 g q6h
Cefepime 2 g q8h
Levofloxacin 750 mg daily
Ceftriaxone plus azithromycin
options.why: Does not cover Pseudomonas, which HAP regimens need.

steps.q: When would you add a second antipseudomonal agent and MRSA coverage?

options.t: Septic shock, ventilation, IV antibiotics in the past 90 days, or high local resistance
Always
7 days
21 days

cases.pearl: **HAP: antipseudomonal single agent unless high risk. 7 days.**

sources.t: Kalil AC, et al. IDSA/ATS HAP and VAP guideline. Clin Infect Dis 2016;63:e61-e111

cases.title: Cefepime and confusion
cases.stem: A 79 year old on cefepime 2 g every 8 hours, CrCl 25 mL/min, is newly confused with jerking movements.

options.t: Cefepime neurotoxicity from accumulation in kidney impairment (can include nonconvulsive status epilepticus)
options.why: FDA 2012 alert: most cases had kidney impairment without dose adjustment.

options.t: Normal aging
Reduce or change the antibiotic per renal dosing, tell the team, and suggest an EEG if seizures are suspected
options.why: Symptoms usually improve after stopping or adjusting the dose.

options.t: Add haloperidol and continue
options.why: Treats the symptom, not the cause.

cases.pearl: **Confused on cefepime with poor kidneys: think drug, adjust the dose (CrCl 60 or less).**

sources.t: FDA safety alert: cefepime and nonconvulsive status epilepticus in kidney impairment (2012)

cases.title: Pyelonephritis and complicated UTI
cases.setting: Med surg · fever and flank pain
cases.stem: Pyelonephritis, no sepsis. No fluoroquinolone in the past year.

options.t: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily
A fluoroquinolone (if not used in the past 12 months and local resistance allows)
Nitrofurantoin
options.why: Does not reach the kidneys or blood. Not for cUTI or pyelonephritis.

options.t: Oral fosfomycin
7 days (5 to 7 with a fluoroquinolone), including with bacteremia
14 days for everyone

steps.q: She improves on day 2 and the E. coli is susceptible. Next step?

options.t: Switch to an oral option by susceptibility (for example TMP SMX DS BID, levofloxacin, cephalexin 1 g TID or amoxicillin clavulanate)
Keep IV for 14 days

cases.pearl: **cUTI: ceftriaxone or FQ, 7 days, oral step down. No nitrofurantoin or fosfomycin for pyelo.**

sources.t: Trautner BW, et al. IDSA 2025 guideline on complicated UTI. Clin Infect Dis 2025

cases.title: The positive urine culture
cases.stem: An 84 year old admitted after a fall, mildly confused, no fever, no urinary symptoms. Urine culture grows E. coli. Ciprofloxacin is ordered.

options.t: Asymptomatic bacteriuria: do not treat
options.why: Confusion or a fall without urinary or systemic signs is not a reason to treat (IDSA 2019).

options.t: A UTI that needs 14 days of antibiotics

steps.q: When IS asymptomatic bacteriuria screened and treated?

options.t: Pregnancy (4 to 7 days)
Before a urologic procedure with mucosal trauma
Older adults with a catheter

cases.pearl: **Bugs without symptoms = no antibiotics (except pregnancy and urology procedures).**

sources.t: AAFP: asymptomatic bacteriuria (IDSA 2019 guideline summary)

cases.title: Cellulitis or abscess?
cases.stem: Two patients: (A) red, warm, spreading leg, no pus; (B) a 3 cm fluctuant abscess on the thigh.

steps.q: Best plan for patient A (mild, nonpurulent)?

options.t: Cephalexin 500 mg QID (or 1 g q8h) for about 5 days
options.why: Nonpurulent cellulitis is usually strep; MRSA coverage is not routine.

options.t: TMP SMX alone
Incision and drainage first; add TMP SMX DS or doxycycline because it is over 2 cm
Antibiotics only, no drainage

cases.pearl: **No pus: strep coverage. Pus: drain it, then MRSA coverage if over 2 cm.**

sources.t: Stevens DL, et al. IDSA skin and soft tissue infection guideline. Clin Infect Dis 2014;59:e10-e52

cases.title: Bacterial meningitis
cases.stem: A 34 year old with suspected bacterial meningitis. No allergies.

options.t: Vancomycin plus ceftriaxone 2 g IV every 12 hours
options.why: Note meningitis dosing of ceftriaxone is every 12 hours.

options.t: Ceftriaxone 1 g daily alone
options.why: Too low and missing resistant pneumococcus coverage.

options.t: 10 to 20 minutes before or with the first antibiotic dose, 0.15 mg/kg every 6 hours for 2 to 4 days; continue only if pneumococcal
After 24 hours of antibiotics

steps.q: If she were 60 years old, what would you add?

options.t: Ampicillin 2 g IV every 4 hours for Listeria
options.why: Also for pregnancy and immunocompromise. Cephalosporins never cover Listeria.

options.t: Nothing

cases.pearl: **Meningitis: vanc + ceftriaxone 2 g q12h, dex before or with dose 1, add ampicillin if over 50.**

sources.t: Tunkel AR, et al. IDSA bacterial meningitis guideline. Clin Infect Dis 2004;39:1267-1284

cases.title: S. aureus in the blood
cases.stem: Blood cultures grow MSSA (methicillin susceptible S. aureus). The patient is on vancomycin.

options.t: Switch to cefazolin or an antistaphylococcal penicillin (nafcillin or oxacillin)
options.why: Beta lactams kill MSSA better than vancomycin.

options.t: Continue vancomycin because it covers MSSA
options.why: It covers it, but outcomes are worse than with a beta lactam.

steps.q: What else always goes with S. aureus bacteremia?

options.t: Repeat blood cultures to document clearance
Infectious diseases consultation and a search for the source (echocardiogram)
At least 14 days of IV therapy from the first negative culture for uncomplicated cases
A 5 day oral course

cases.pearl: **S. aureus in blood: never a contaminant. Beta lactam for MSSA, repeat cultures, ID, echo, 14 days or more.**

sources.t: Liu C, et al. IDSA MRSA guideline. Clin Infect Dis 2011;52:e18-e55
St. Mary's antibiogram, sepsis order set and antimicrobial stewardship policies (verify locally)

cases.title: ESBL in the blood
cases.stem: Blood cultures: E. coli resistant to ceftriaxone (ESBL producer). The patient is on piperacillin tazobactam, and it tests susceptible.

options.t: Change to a carbapenem (for example meropenem or ertapenem)
options.why: MERINO: 30 day mortality was higher with piperacillin tazobactam than meropenem for ceftriaxone resistant E. coli and Klebsiella bacteremia.

options.t: Continue piperacillin tazobactam because it tested susceptible
options.why: The trial showed worse outcomes despite susceptibility.

sources.t: Harris PNA, et al. Piperacillin tazobactam vs meropenem for ceftriaxone resistant E. coli or Klebsiella bacteremia (MERINO). JAMA 2018;320:984-994
St. Mary's antibiogram, sepsis order set and antimicrobial stewardship policies (verify locally)

cases.title: Penicillin allergy label
cases.stem: Allergy: "penicillin, hives 20 years ago." Cefazolin 2 g is ordered for surgical prophylaxis. The surgeon asks for vancomycin "to be safe."

steps.q: What do you know about cefazolin and penicillin cross reactivity?

options.t: Cefazolin shares no side chain with other US beta lactams; cross reactivity is very low
options.why: Allergy is driven by the R1 side chain, not the beta lactam ring.

options.t: Up to 10% cross reactivity with all cephalosporins
Give cefazolin; it is a better surgical prophylaxis agent than vancomycin
options.why: With a non anaphylactic, unconfirmed history, cephalosporins can be given without testing (2022 practice parameter). Vancomycin is less effective for MSSA and takes longer to infuse.

options.t: Vancomycin for everyone with a penicillin label

steps.q: What is the cefazolin prophylaxis dose and timing?

options.t: 2 g IV (3 g if 120 kg or more) within 60 minutes before incision; redose every 4 hours during surgery
options.why: Vancomycin needs to start within 120 minutes because of its long infusion.

options.t: 1 g after surgery
options.why: Prophylaxis must be on board at incision.

cases.pearl: **Penicillin hives: cefazolin is fine. 2 g (3 g if 120 kg+) within 60 minutes of incision.**

sources.t: Brameli, Stone, Phillips. J Allergy Clin Immunol Glob 2024 (cites the 2022 drug allergy practice parameter)
Nebraska Medicine: surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis guideline
St. Mary's antibiogram, sepsis order set and antimicrobial stewardship policies (verify locally)

cases.title: Duplicate anaerobic coverage
cases.stem: Orders: piperacillin tazobactam 4.5 g q6h plus metronidazole 500 mg q8h.

options.t: Duplicate anaerobic coverage: piperacillin tazobactam already covers anaerobes
options.why: Same with carbapenems. Metronidazole adds side effects without benefit (except C. difficile, which needs oral therapy).

options.t: No issue

cases.call: "Piperacillin tazobactam already covers anaerobes. May I stop the metronidazole?"
cases.pearl: **Pip tazo or a carbapenem + metronidazole = double anaerobes.**

sources.t: St. Mary's antibiogram, sepsis order set and antimicrobial stewardship policies (verify locally)

cases.title: Day 3 antibiotic time out
cases.stem: You review every patient on antibiotics for day 3.

steps.q: What questions do you ask on each one?

options.t: Are cultures back, and can we narrow?
Can we switch to oral?
Is there a stop date that matches guideline durations?
options.why: CAP 5 days, HAP 7, cUTI 7, cellulitis about 5.

options.t: Can we add more coverage just in case?

sources.t: Metlay JP, et al. ATS/IDSA community acquired pneumonia guideline. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2019;200:e45-e67
Kalil AC, et al. IDSA/ATS HAP and VAP guideline. Clin Infect Dis 2016;63:e61-e111
Trautner BW, et al. IDSA 2025 guideline on complicated UTI. Clin Infect Dis 2025

cases.title: Shift simulation: ID calls
cases.stem: Three items: (1) a new meningitis patient needs first doses; (2) an MSSA bacteremia patient is still on vancomycin; (3) a question about cephalexin dosing for discharge tomorrow.

options.t: The meningitis first doses (and dexamethasone timing)
The MSSA switch
Discharge question
Recommend switching MSSA bacteremia to cefazolin
Discharge question

cases.pearl: **Meningitis now, MSSA switch next, discharge questions last.**
